problem:
$$
V=\text{Span}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]},\,B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V,$ given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
worked_solution:
First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{5\cdot 2+0\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B={{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}$ is an orthogonal basis for $V.$

Finally, $a=3,$ $b=2,$ and  

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$
